// diagnostic

E0065

This function uses the retired `::` or legacy `=` body marker.

What

This function uses the retired `::` or legacy `=` body marker.

Why

A one-expression function body uses `->`; `::` binds a name, and `=` fills a slot inside a definition.

Fix

Replace the marker with `->`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0065: tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.stderr.

Error [E0068]: this callable uses the retired result-arrow shape.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:7:36
    |
  7 | fn Incrementer.apply(self, x: I32) -[]> I32 :: x + 1
    |                                    ^
 Why: a return type sits after the parameter list, and `->` introduces the body; an effect ceiling follows the return type
 Fix: write `fn name(...) Type -> body`, or `fn name(...) Type -[Effects]> { … }`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0068

Error [E0065]: this function uses the retired `::` body marker.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:7:45
    |
  7 | fn Incrementer.apply(self, x: I32) -[]> I32 :: x + 1
    |                                             ^^
 Why: A one-expression function body uses `->`; `::` binds a name, and `=` fills a slot inside a definition.
 Fix: replace `::` with `->`; `jet fmt` applies this fix.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0065

Error [E0302]: `Incrementer` has no field `apply`
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:15:22
    |
 15 |     print(c.call(inc.apply, 1))
    |                      ^^^^^
 Why: field access only works on names declared in the struct
 Fix: check the field names on `Incrementer`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0302

Error [E3203]: `fn(I32) I32 -[]>` is not a C-compatible type for a foreign function parameter or return.
  --> tests/ui/cffi_callback_bound_method.jet:15:22
    |
 15 |     print(c.call(inc.apply, 1))
    |                      ^^^^^
 Why: `#Extern` / `#Bindgen` functions must use types with a stable C ABI at the edge.
 Fix: use scalars, `String`, or a struct with C layout; pointers only through the gated tier.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3203
